newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists seal accords with leftist groups.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists seal accords with leftist groups.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists said on Wednesday they had sealed accords with the small Greens and Radical-Socialist groups ahead of general elections due early next year, but talks with a third left-wing party had failed.

Daniel Vaillant, deputy-head of the Socialist Party, blamed excessive demands by the small Citizens' Movement of former defence minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement, chiefly the dropping of plans for a single European currency, for the failure.
The deal agreed with the Radical-Socialists stipulates a minimum of 35 constituencies in which they will put forward a candidate backed by the Socialists and the Greens.

The agreement reached with the Greens, the first-ever such deal, provides similar conditions for some 30 constituencies, Vaillant said, adding that issues including policy proposals had yet to be decided.
In exchange, the environmentalists pledged not to put forward candidates against the two left-wing partners in 100 or so of the country's 577 constituencies.
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin appealed to other leftist forces last week to forge a pact "to govern together".
But he insisted his party would not give up the single European currency, a caution chiefly addressed to the second-biggest left-wing force, the Communists.
The Communists, who oppose the single currency and insist on a referendum on the issue, have vowed to put pressure on the Socialists to rally to their views.
France narrowly approved the European monetary union in a 1992 referendum.
